subject: maths
question: Deepa deposited Rs. 10,000 in a bank on simple interest. After 4 years, she received an amount of Rs. 12,400. Find the rate of interest.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total Simple Interest (SI) = 12,400 − 10,000 = Rs. 2,400

SI for 1 year = 2,400 ÷ 4 = Rs. 600

Rate of Interest (R) = (SI for 1 year ÷ Principal) × 100

⇒ R = (600 ÷ 10000) × 100 = 6%

**∴ The correct answer is 6% p.a.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Principal (P) = Rs. 10,000

Amount (A) = Rs. 12,400

Time (T) = 4 years

 
• 
 
 
 0 Years
 P = ₹10,000
 
 
 4 Years
 A = ₹12,400
 
 

 

 
 
 + SI = ₹2,400

 SI per year = ₹2400 ÷ 4 = ₹600

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = Amount (A) − Principal (P)

SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

**Calculations:**

⇒ SI = 12400 − 10000 = Rs. 2400

⇒ 2400 = (10000 × R × 4) ÷ 100

⇒ 2400 = 100 × R × 4

⇒ 2400 = 400 × R

⇒ R = 2400 ÷ 400

⇒ R = 6

**∴ The correct answer is 6% p.a.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Difference between SI and CI

Simple Interest is calculated only on the principal amount, while Compound Interest is calculated on the principal as well as the accumulated interest.

SI vs CI for 2 Years

The difference between Compound Interest and Simple Interest on the same principal for 2 years is given by: Difference = P(R ÷ 100)²

Rule of 72

A quick way to estimate the number of years required to double your money at a given annual fixed interest rate (R) is approximately 72 ÷ R.
